chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
It is not allowed for the man that he sits cross-legged facing the Kabah.

key_terms.الْكَعْبَةِ: the Ka'bah (the cube-shaped building in Mecca)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a man to sit cross-legged facing the Ka'bah?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a specific etiquette (adab) for men, prohibiting the cross-legged posture (ihtibā) directly facing the Ka'bah, distinguishing it from the general orientation of prayer (qiblah). In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling is often discussed in the context of distinguishing between acts of worship and general reverence, with some scholars noting its applicability to voluntary acts or specific contexts of sitting in the Masjid al-Haram. It underscores the importance of bodily humility and decorum when in the presence of the holiest site.
